title: Escape resource and annotation keys before constructing JSONPatch paths
answers: Why can GPU pods bypass VPA resource caps?
How should extended resource names be encoded in admission patches?
How do I escape annotation names containing slash or tilde?
body:
Symptom: Pods requesting extended resources such as GPUs can bypass VPA resource caps when admission patches fail and webhook failures are ignored.
Root cause: vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/admission-controller/resource/pod/patch/util.go:GetAddResourceRequirementValuePatch inserted resource names directly into JSONPatch paths, treating slashes inside names as path separators.
Fix pattern: Use vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/admission-controller/resource/pod/patch/util.go:escapeJSONPatchPath on each raw key segment before interpolation; replace ~ with ~0 first, then / with ~1, so nvidia.com/gpu becomes nvidia.com~1gpu.
Constraints: Escape individual key segments, not the complete path. Resource names and annotation names share this encoding through GetAddResourceRequirementValuePatch, GetAddAnnotationPatch and GetRemoveAnnotationPatch in vertical-pod-autoscaler/pkg/admission-controller/resource/pod/patch/util.go; structural separators and standard cpu/memory names remain unchanged.
applies: VPA admission-controller JSONPatch construction for container resource requirements and annotation additions or removals.
